name: Bomra's
must_try: scotch egg with manipuri black rice
why_it_matters: Goa's only serious modern-Burmese kitchen, founded by chef Bawmra Jap (originally from Myanmar) in Candolim in 2003 and relocated to a heritage Anjuna villa as the second iteration. Listed on the World's 50 Best Discovery and ranked No. 5 on the Condé Nast Traveller x Zomato Top Restaurant Awards 2024. The chef still runs the kitchen garden personally; the khow suey and crackling-pork salad are the dishes regulars fly down for.
insider_tip: Look for the scarlet rickshaw outside the gate — that's the Anjuna landmark. Book the al-fresco terrace for dinner; the inside dining room fills up first because of the air-conditioning, but the terrace is where the place actually breathes.
signature_address: 1152, opp. Our Lady Of Health Chapel, Mazal Waddo, Anjuna, Goa 403509

name: Edible Archives
must_try: grilled beef salad with pineapple and sprouts
korean egg with manipuri black rice
why_it_matters: Chef Anumitra Ghosh Dastidar's research-led restaurant, run with partner Shalini Krishan inside a century-old Goan house. The kitchen began as a project for the 2018-19 Kochi-Muziris Biennale and now works almost exclusively with indigenous Indian rice varieties — the menu pulls from Bengali, Goan, Japanese, Thai and Northeastern technique. Won Gold at the Outlook Traveller Responsible Tourism Awards 2025 (Food category) and is regularly cited by Condé Nast Traveller India among the country's best restaurants.
insider_tip: Order the rice flight if it's on — it's the cleanest way to taste why this kitchen exists. Lunch is a calmer, lighter window than dinner; the chef sometimes comes out to walk you through the day's grain.

name: Hosa
must_try: tellicherry pepper crab roast with garlic butter
why_it_matters: Modern South Indian fine-dining room from EHV (the Indian Accent group), opened in late 2022 inside a high-ceilinged Portuguese villa overlooking the Anjuna river. Chef Suresh DC travelled across south India to build the menu; listed on the World's 50 Best Discovery and one of very few Goa restaurants on Condé Nast Traveller India's Top Restaurant Awards short-list. Hosa means 'new' in Kannada — the brief is south Indian regional cooking pushed beyond the dosa-and-idli stereotype.
insider_tip: Ask for the dining terrace, not the indoor room — the river view at sunset is the whole point. The vegetarian tasting menu is unusually strong; even committed carnivores order it as a parallel side.
signature_address: Irada Home, House No. 60/1, near St Anthony's Church, Vaddy, Siolim, Bardez, Goa 403517

name: Ciao Bella
why_it_matters: Long-running Italian garden restaurant run by Italian couple Simona and Mario, tucked off the Anjuna-Mapusa road in Assagao. One of the oldest Italian rooms in north Goa and still the inland cluster's benchmark for honest, owner-cooked pasta and Naples-style pizza. Repeat-customer rate is the real signal — the same Bombay weekenders have been booking the same garden table for nearly two decades.
insider_tip: Sit in the garden, not the indoor room — the place is built around it. Reservations are essential on weekend evenings; walk-ins routinely get turned away from 8pm onwards in season.
signature_address: House No. 283, Badem, Assagao, Bardez, Goa 403507

name: Olive Bar & Kitchen
why_it_matters: AD Singh's Olive Bar & Kitchen relocated its Goa flagship to a clifftop spot above Big Vagator beach in 2018 — all-white walls, Arabian sea on one side, sunset on the other. Named to the Condé Nast Traveller Hot List 2019 and to CNT's Best Beach Clubs in the World list for both Summer 2024 and Summer 2025. Head chef Dhruv Oberoi runs a Mediterranean-coastal menu that's the inland-cluster default for an anniversary or a slow Sunday.
insider_tip: Sunday brunch is the move — bottomless wine, live music, and the only Olive seating where you can hear the Arabian sea. Book the cliff-edge tables (3, 4 or 5) at least a week ahead in season.
signature_address: Unit 1, Vagator Helipad, Big Vagator, Anjuna, Bardez, Goa 403509

name: Gunpowder
why_it_matters: Founder Satish Warier ran the original Gunpowder out of Delhi's Hauz Khas Village from 2009, then moved the kitchen full-time to a Portuguese-era house in Assagao in 2013, sharing the compound with the People Tree design collective. The 'Peninsular Kitchen' brief — Kerala, Andhra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka — is rigorous and regional, not a generic south-Indian sampler. Twelve years on, it's still the inland cluster's reference for what coastal south Indian cooking actually tastes like.
insider_tip: Closed Mondays and only does dinner six days a week — most disappointed reviews are people who turned up at 5pm. Order the appam-stew combo even if you came for the beef fry; it's the dish the kitchen is quietly proudest of.
signature_address: House No. 645, Anjuna-Mapusa Road, Badem, Assagao, Bardez, Goa 403507

name: Avo's Kitchen
why_it_matters: 'Avo' means grandmother in Konkani — and the brief is exactly that: home-style Goan food cooked the way a Bardez avo would, in a bright Assagao bungalow. The fish thali, recheado-stuffed mackerel and prawn forminhas are the dishes Bombay weekenders order three days running. Earned a spot on Tripadvisor's top-tier Assagao list for three consecutive years and now a fixture on the inland-Goa lunch circuit alongside Gunpowder and Sublime.
insider_tip: It opens at 12:30pm and the thali sells through by 3pm in season — go early. The garden seating is small; if you want a long lazy lunch, ask for the back room with the cane chairs.
signature_address: House No. 47, Anjuna-Mapusa Road, Saunta Vaddo, Assagao, Bardez, Goa 403507
